source_text:
Ἀρχὴ δὲ πάντων χαλεπῶν φιλαργυρία. εἰδότες οὖν ὅτι οὐδὲν εἰσηνέγκαμεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον, ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ ἐξενεγκεῖν τι ἔχομεν, ὁπλισώμεθα τοῖς ὅπλοις τῆς δικαιοσύνης καὶ διδάξωμεν ἑαυτοὺς πρῶτον πορεύεσθαι ἐν τῇ ἐντολῇ τοῦ κυριοῦ:
ἔπειτα καὶ τὰς γυναῖκας ἡμῶν ἐν τῇ δοθείσῃ αὐταῖς πίστει καὶ ἀγάπῃ καὶ ἁγνείᾳ στεργούσας τοὺς ἑαυτῶν ἄνδρας ἐν πάσῃ ἀληθείᾳ καὶ ἀγαπώσας πάντας ἐξ ἴσου ἐν πάσῃ ἐγκρατείᾳ, καὶ τὰ τέκνα παιδεύειν τὴν παιδείαν τοῦ φόβου τοῦ θεοῦ:
τὰς χήρας σωφρονούσας περὶ τὴν τοῦ κυρίου πίστιν, ἐντυγχανούσας ἀδιαλείπτως περὶ πάντων, μακρὰν οὔσας πάσης διαβολῆς, καταλαλιᾶς, ψευδομαρτυρίας, φιλαργυρίας καὶ παντὸς κακοῦ, γινωσκούσας ὅτι εἰσὶ θυσιαστήριον θεοῦ καὶ ὅτι πάντα μωμοσκοπεῖται, καὶ λέληθεν αὐτὸν οὐδὲν οὔτε λογισμῶν οὔτε ἐννοιῶν οὔτε τι τῶν κρυπτῶν τῆς καρδίας.
thought_title: The root of evils and the duties of wives and widows
orientation: Polycarp is opening his letter by urging the Philippians to take up the weapons of righteousness, beginning with themselves and then their wives and widows.
pass_a_gloss: But the beginning of all hard things is love of money. Knowing therefore that we brought nothing into the world, but neither do we have anything to carry out, let us arm ourselves with the weapons of righteousness and let us teach ourselves first to walk in the commandment of the Lord: then also our wives, in the faith and love and purity given to them, loving their own husbands in all truth and loving all equally in all self-control, and to teach the children the discipline of the fear of God: the widows being self-controlled concerning the faith of the Lord, interceding unceasingly for all, being far from all slander, evil-speaking, false witness, love of money and every evil, knowing that they are an altar of God and that all things are examined, and nothing is hidden from him, neither of reasonings nor of thoughts nor any of the hidden things of the heart.

choices.why: Glossary term; renders the compound literally as love of money, avoiding the banned 'avarice' and 'greed'.

choices.english: let us arm ourselves with the weapons of righteousness
choices.why: Keeps the cognate verb-noun pair (arm ourselves with weapons) and the glossary term righteousness.
rejected: let us put on the armor of righteousness

choices.term: πορεύεσθαι ἐν τῇ ἐντολῇ τοῦ κυρίου
choices.english: to walk in the commandment of the Lord
choices.why: Preserves the literal 'walk' metaphor and the singular commandment, matching the source.
rejected: to live according to the Lord's command

choices.why: Glossary term; keeps the anarthrous predicate as indefinite, matching the Greek.
Renders the rare verb literally as passive examination, preserving the idea of scrutiny.
Keeps the perfect of λανθάνω with the dative of person as 'hidden from him', preserving the negation.

bible_refs.note: οὐδὲν εἰσηνέγκαμεν εἰς τὸν κόσμον, ἀλλ’ οὐδὲ ἐξενεγκεῖν τι ἔχομεν

pass_b_english: The love of money is the beginning of all troubles. Since we know that we brought nothing into the world, and we can take nothing out of it, let us arm ourselves with the weapons of righteousness and first teach ourselves to walk in the commandment of the Lord.

Then teach our wives to love their own husbands in all truth, in the faith and love and purity given to them, and to love everyone equally with all self-control, and to raise their children in the discipline of the fear of God.

Teach the widows to be self-controlled in the faith of the Lord, to intercede constantly for everyone, to keep far from all slander, gossip, false witness, love of money, and every evil, knowing that they are an altar of God and that everything is examined, and nothing is hidden from him—neither reasonings nor thoughts nor any of the secrets of the heart.

last_rejected.quote: The love of money is the beginning of all troubles
last_rejected.why: Source says 'of all difficult/hard things' not 'troubles'; 'χαλεπῶν' means difficult, grievous, severe, not merely 'troubles'
last_rejected.fix: The love of money is the beginning of all hardships
last_rejected.ruling: χαλεπῶν means troublesome/difficult; 'troubles' captures the sense adequately for readers.

last_rejected.quote: Then teach our wives to love their own husbands
last_rejected.why: Missing 'στεργούσας' (cherishing/affection) distinct from 'ἀγαπώσας' (loving); English collapses both into 'love'
last_rejected.fix: Then teach our wives to cherish their own husbands and to love everyone equally
last_rejected.ruling: στεργούσας and ἀγαπώσας both fall within 'love'; distinction is nuance, not meaning loss.

last_rejected.quote: nothing is hidden from him—neither reasonings nor thoughts
last_rejected.source_quote: λέληθεν αὐτὸν οὐδὲν οὔτε λογισμῶν οὔτε ἐννοιῶν
last_rejected.why: λέληθεν is 'escapes him'/'is unnoticed by him' with dative; 'nothing is hidden from him' reverses agency—things don't hide from God, God doesn't miss things
last_rejected.fix: and nothing escapes him—neither reasonings nor thoughts
last_rejected.ruling: 'Nothing is hidden from him' correctly conveys λέληθεν αὐτὸν οὐδέν; agency nuance is not misleading.
